questions.question: Eight teachers Anil, Kamal, Ram, Sanjay, Aakash, Vivek, Rahul and Ramu are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Ramu is third to the left of Ram. Vivek is third to the right of Ram. Aakash is to the immediate right of Anil. Sanjay is not the immediate neighbour of Ram or Ramu. Rahul is second to the left of Anil. Who is second to the left of Kamal?
questions.solution:
Given: Eight teachers Anil, Kamal, Ram, Sanjay, Aakash, Vivek, Rahul and Ram.

1) Ramu is third to the left of Ram.

2) Vivek is third to the right of Ram.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/248be91eea2c6177bb8baaa55172b7a93dcd5398dcf9b8b9771218a425ce6f38.png] 

3) Sanjay is not the immediate neighbour of Ram or Ramu.

4) Aakash is to the immediate right of Anil.

5) Rahul is second to the left of Anil.

And, Kamal will sit on the remaining place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3e6bd815e2051c169b2067069a8437db5d0ed39b837844aba8b06782593eefd.png] 

Here, 'Aakash' is second to the left of Kamal.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some L are M.

II. All G are M.

**Conclusion:**

I. No G is L.

II. No M is L.

III. Some M are G.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows
Both conclusions I and III follows

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. Some L are M.

II. All G are M.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9984acdc2ec67f97915cb741188d79f7fdb10f55da30f4eb14d951119401df54.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No G is L - False (Because, No definite relation given between G and L, so it can be possible only).

II. No M is L - False (Because, Some L are M).

III. Some M are G - True (Because, All G are M gives Some M are G).

So, Only conclusion III follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
After interchanging which two signs, the value of the given equation will be '1'?

12 × 6 - 28 + 3 ÷ 9
questions.solution:
Given equation: 12 × 6 - 28 + 3 ÷ 9 = 1.

BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Let's check each option one by one.

Option 1) × and +

Given: 12 × 6 - 28 + 3 ÷ 9 = 1

After interchanging the signs we get;

⇒ 12 + 6 - __**28 × 3 ÷ 9**__ = 1

⇒ __**12 + 6**__ - 9.33 = 1

⇒ __18 - 9.33__ = 1

⇒ 8.67 ≠ 1

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) + and -

Given: 12 × 6 - 28 + 3 ÷ 9 = 1

After interchanging the signs we get;

⇒ 12 × 6 + 28 - __**3 ÷ 9**__ = 1

⇒ __**12 × 6**__ + 28 - 0.33 = 1

⇒ __**72 + 28**__ - 0.33 = 1

⇒ __**100 - 0.33**__ = 1

⇒ 99.67 ≠ 1

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) **÷ and ×**

Given: 12 × 6 - 28 + 3 ÷ 9 = 1

After interchanging the signs we get;

⇒ __**12 ÷ 6**__ - 28 + 3 × 9 = 1

⇒ 2 - 28 + __**3 × 9**__ = 1

⇒ __**2**__ - 28 __**+ 27**__ = 1

⇒ __29** - 28**__ = 1

⇒ **1** = 1

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 4) × and -

Given: 12 × 6 - 28 + 3 ÷ 9 = 1

After interchanging the signs we get;

⇒ 12 - 6 × 28 + __**3 ÷ 9**__ = 1

⇒ 12 - __**6 × 28**__ + 0.33 = 1

⇒ __**12**__ - 168 __**+ 0.33**__ = 1

⇒ __12.33** - 168**__ = 1

⇒ 155.67 ≠ 1

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'BADAM' is written as '69760', 'JBDN' is written as '0849', 'CANDY' is written as '39654'. How is 'B' written in that code language?
questions.solution:
Given:

'BADAM' is written as '69760',

'JBDN' is written as '0849',

'CANDY' is written as '39654'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba813de95f76ce8dc0f72f9715bf5ead7defd3e00fba59dcbb611a8a2223ec1a.png] 

Here,

'0' is the code for 'B'.

'6' is the code for 'A'.

'9' is the code for 'D'.

'7' is the code for 'M'.

'4' is the code for 'N'.

'8' is the code for 'J'.

Either '3' or '5' is the code for either 'C' or 'Y'.

So, 'B' will be coded as '0'.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: Speed of six bikes T1, T2, T3, T4, T5 and T6 are compared. Speed of T6 is more than only three bikes. No two bikes have same speed. Speed of T4 is more than T2 but less than T6. Speed of T3 is not less than T5. Speed of T2 and T5 is not least. How many bikes have less speed than T3?
questions.solution:
Given: Six bikes T1, T2, T3, T4, T5 and T6.

1) Speed of T6 is more than only three bikes.

__ > __ > T6 > __ > __ > __ 

2) Speed of T4 is more than T2 but less than T6.

3) Speed of T2 and T5 is not least.

__ > __ > T6 > T4 > T2 > __ 

4) Speed of T3 is not less than T5.

T3 > T5 > T6 > T4 > T2 > __ 

And, T1 is placed at the remaining place.

T3 > T5 > T6 > T4 > T2 > T1

Here, there are '5' bikes have less speed than T3.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.
